items.title: Irwin Leclere Interview, 1970-04-14
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did you play any other rags by Joplin or James Scott or? [INTERVIEWEE] No, no there was a fellow by the name of Piron...

ctx.x: Well they played all the singing, you know, they used to always have singers in the cafes, and of course they played jazz too, I say jazz, that's what they call it now, but ragtime they used to call it in those days. When you played jazz they'd call it, well it plays ragtime, you see. Well would you play, say, Maple Leaf Rag? Yeah, Maple Leaf Rag, and Weisdorf used to play that wonderfully.
Did you play any other rags by Joplin or James Scott or?

No, no there was a fellow by the name of Piron, he was a car fellow, Almond Puyla, what was his first name? Almond J. Piron. Yeah, Almond J. Piron. And he wrote a song, Purple Rose of Cairo, and I wrote the second part of it, and we never had it published. You wrote the second part of that? Yeah. It's out?
